title: Pop! Goes the Weasel
description: Your photographed 16-measure arrangement in 3/4. Preserve the rests and hold tied left-hand chords without striking them again. In measure 13, cross the left hand over to play G-sharp4 and A4 together (fingers 2 and 1). Printed fingerings, phrasing, staccatos and dynamics are shown. The source says Lively without a numerical tempo; start at 60 BPM and adjust comfortably. BPM counts quarter notes.

title: Prelude in C major · BWV 924
description: All 18 measures from your four unique score images. Main-note practice edition: the ornament symbols are retained for reference, but MIDI grading and Listen use the main written notes only. Omit ornament embellishments during graded practice. In measures 9–10 the hands alternate across the staves: the thumb-led groups belong to RH, and the groups beginning with finger 4 belong to LH. Hand selection and note hints follow these handoffs. Hold the tied left-hand G octave from measure 11 through measure 17 without re-striking it. Measure 17 has two independent right-hand voices. Printed fingerings are included where clear; the original images include the ornament explanations. Play at your own pace; Listen uses the printed quarter note = 69.

title: 1. Minuet in G major · BWV Anh. 114
description: Minuet in G from the Anna Magdalena Bach notebook, BWV Anh. 114. Transcribed from your photograph with its printed fingerings, articulation and independent left-hand voices. Both 16-bar sections repeat: the 32 printed bars are written out as 64 practice measures (A A B B). The small A grace note in source bar 8 is realized as a short sixteenth before G, within the beat. Start hands separately at 66 quarter-note BPM. The printed dotted-half = 66 is a faster performance indication, equivalent to 198 quarter-note BPM; the practice tempo is deliberately slower.
learningFocus: Three-beat pulse, half-beats, phrasing and independent hands.
